qualification: Notify published guest block completions while other I/O continues

regression.scenario: Three ordinary reads with two transfer cells. Completing the first read frees a cell and admits the third; the first used entry must notify the guest before either later read completes.
regression.before: Production backend test failed the interrupt-count assertion
regression.after: PASS for successful and failed first reads; separate partial-chunk test proves no early interrupt and one final-completion interrupt

gate.result: PASS, followed by target drain test in successful exit-0 pipeline

target_drain.result: PASS: accepted pending request completed with empty queues and interrupts suppressed during drain

intel_regression.host: Existing Intel Linux host madmax, accessed through puck.local
intel_regression.ssh: Existing key-only identity; original Ed25519 host key from agentos-qemu-LxAV1n.known_hosts; loopback port 12224
intel_regression.result: PASS, exit 0: pinned-host-key public-key SSH, x86_64 identity and sync

limits: The three-request interrupt assertion is a host test of the production backend with interrupt injection mocked.
The OS gate and drain test prove target regressions pass, not an on-target interrupt-latency bound.
Intel SSH is a boot/I/O regression check, not guest recreation, concurrent disk isolation or a measured interrupt-latency result.
This is not yet established as the cause or fix of the seeded Debian second-boot failure; no persistence or performance improvement claim.
